second_tier_references.title: An Improved Vortex Lattice Method for Nonstationary Problems
A Compilation of the Mathematics Leading to the Doublet Lattice Method
second_tier_references.abstract: This report provides a theoretical development of the doublet lattice method, the method of choice for most subsonic unsteady aerodynamic modelling for over twenty years. This is a tutorial based on many-key mathematical developments provided in the References section. An example source code is provided in the Appendix.

primary_paper.title: Calculation of supersonic viscous flow over delta wings with sharp subsonic leading edges
primary_paper.abstract: Two complementary procedures were developed to calculate the viscous supersonic flow over conical shapes at large angles of attack, with application to cones and delta wings. In the first approach the flow is assumed to be conical and the governing equations are solved at a given Reynolds number with a time-marching explicit finite-difference algorithm. In the second method the parabolized Navier-Stokes equations are solved with a space-marching implicit noniterative finite-difference algorithm. This latter approach is not restricted to conical shapes and provides a large improvement in computational efficiency over published methods. Results from the two procedures agree very well with each other and with available experimental data.
